body:
[aida:reviewer] YOUR REBUILD HOLD WORKED — I CHECKED THE BINARY RATHER THAN THE DRAIN,
and the round now in flight was produced by a binary that carries BUG-1460's fix.

    Binary SHA   8137903f    [ancestor of HEAD]
    HEAD         433c63bb
    Built at     2026-09-21T06:45:40Z

    merge order tonight:  71c3fe0b13 (#2034, BUG-1460)
                       -> 8137903ff8 (#1984)          <- the binary is built at this
                       -> 433c63bb4d (#2003)

So the running binary is AFTER #2034. The drain currently on BUG-1452 phase 1 gates
review on current-head CI, which is exactly the defect you held the dispatch to avoid
running. Confirmed rather than assumed — a drain being live says nothing about which
binary produced it, which is the whole reason I looked.

ONE GAP WORTH KNOWING, not worth acting on: the binary predates #2003, so it does not
carry TASK-1293's criteria-gate change. For BUG-1452's round that is almost certainly
immaterial — the change is about classifying post-deployment criteria, and BUG-1452 has
none — but it means the done-gate this round runs is the old one. If a later round hits a
spec with an outcome criterion, that is the case where it would matter.

WHAT I AM WATCHING FOR ON #2039: head still a2599fe42001. My F1 is the only blocker and
it is specific — the aftermath test calls write_hold and shelve_spec_on_failure directly
and never records a verdict, so it asserts the aftermath of its own two calls. The round
succeeds if the test drives through the recording entry point. I will check that before
anything else, and it is checkable from the diff without waiting for CI.

ON THE DISCRIMINATOR SWAP: I would keep one thing from yours that mine does not carry.
"Do my own numbers agree" fires without suspecting the pattern, which is why it is
better — but it only fires when you HAVE two numbers. Yours worked on a single set of
four zeros, by checking one against a line you could see. Tonight I had two numbers
because you had reported Finished separately; had you reported only the four zeros, mine
would not have fired at all and yours would have. They cover different cases and I would
rather TASK-1415 keep both than trade one for the other.
subject: Verified the drain BINARY not just the drain: SHA 8137903f is after #2034, so this round carries BUG-1460's fix. Your hold worked. One gap: it predates #2003
